query: Across role, grade level, and subject, which open-response themes are associated with satisfaction?

per_column.name: theme_tech_issues
per_column.rationale: Binary presence flag for a nameable theme; can be grouped and compared against satisfaction. Somewhat rare (14/250) but still yields a meaningful segment.

per_column.name: theme_engagement
per_column.rationale: Interpretable theme flag with well-balanced 76/174 split, ideal for comparing satisfaction across presence/absence.

per_column.name: theme_disengagement
per_column.rationale: Clear semantic theme, 26 positives; supports interpretable segmentation against the focus.

per_column.name: theme_hands_on_need
per_column.rationale: Balanced 91/159 split, nameable theme; strong for exploratory grouping vs satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_teacher_quality
per_column.rationale: Interpretable theme flag with usable segment size (26).

per_column.name: theme_equity_concern
per_column.rationale: Meaningful theme; rare (11) so estimates are noisier, but still an interpretable segment.

per_column.name: theme_flexible_learning
per_column.rationale: Nameable theme, 19 positives; interpretable and groupable against satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_social_connection
per_column.rationale: Well-balanced 92/158 split; excellent for discovering relationships with satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_new_opportunity
per_column.rationale: Interpretable theme flag, 19 positives; supports segmentation.

per_column.name: theme_outcomes_positive
per_column.rationale: Clear valenced theme; groupable and interpretable against the focus.

per_column.name: theme_outcomes_negative
per_column.rationale: Clear valenced theme; complements outcomes_positive for exploratory comparison.

per_column.name: open_response_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categorical variable, but nearly constant (227/250 neutral) and largely a coarse restatement of satisfaction; weak, near-degenerate segmentation.

judge.rationale: The added columns directly realise the exploratory intent: they decompose the free-text open_response into a set of named, human-interpretable themes as binary presence flags that can each be grouped and cross-tabulated against satisfaction, and further sliced by role, grade, and subject. The themes are semantically distinct (tech issues, engagement, teacher quality, equity, social connection, outcomes valence) and several have well-balanced splits (engagement 76/174, hands_on 91/159, social_connection 92/158) supporting robust comparison. Weaknesses: a few themes are quite rare (equity 11, tech 14), making segment estimates noisy, and open_response_sentiment is near-constant (91% neutral) while largely restating the satisfaction signal, so it contributes little interpretive lift. Overall this is a genuine, interpretable relationship-opening set rather than opaque scores, so it substantially satisfies the claim.
